name: Already There
tagline: You can tell who someone will become. You can rarely say how.
epigraph: One grape variety made the grappa here. Grappa was first distilled like that in Friuli.
glassware: small tulip-shaped grappa glass with an open rim (about 150 ml), chilled, no ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v3) and 4-gram pass on whoYouAre and yours: clean against every pour; the epigraph moved off "in this glass comes from" (*innocent-caregiver*) and under 16 words by a lint-only fix to Hester's W1, confirmed by Hester. Never "foresaw", "predicted" or "knew" (C1); no "rescued" or "turned into" (C3); off *For Its Own Good*'s grappa words (C4); no price, Murano or "super-premium" (C5). "I" only; no guest pronouns, archetype names or magic words; never "yours" for the drink. Lint 0 errors, 1 warning: 'she' in yours 2, Giannola Nonino, a historical person, accepted by Wren (r4). ✓

open_items: The fig leaf is the spark and the reach: a guest needs a fig tree, a neighbour's, or a greengrocer who sells the leaves (unsourced). Plain blanc vermouth gives identical numbers but loses the spark; the room didn't mark it optional. The fig-sap caution in the recipe (rinse hands) is unsourced, kept on the safe side; Hester asks Robin for a botanical source. The grappa's strength is unsourced (row 41%); the sweep carries "40% or stronger" (37.5% sits just under the floor). The named bottle is Nonino's young single-varietal (on record, the Picolit Cru); Robin may prefer a style only. Sugar 5.34 g in a 3.7–5.6 band: soft, as a blanc Martini is. The 1967 test bottling and its printed label, the 1973 date and Giannola's quotes are the family's own account ("the family says"). Dossier only, one word: Tomás's closingLine note says "the tree is grown for its fruit" without "mainly" (guest text and Pairings say "mainly"). Veto-free.
